title: Proposal 3: Speed Up Street Safety Projects, Disposition of Unused City Property, and Office Leasing

context.text: This is one of five charter amendment questions placed on the November 2026 ballot by the Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE), the 2026 New York City Charter Revision Commission created by Mayor Zohran Mamdani in May 2026 and chaired by Patrick Gaspard.

question.text: Proposed Charter Amendment: Speed Up Street Safety Projects, Disposition of Unused City Property, Office Leasing. Simplify review of street safety projects to reduce construction timelines. Fast track disposition of unused City property with approval from City Planning Commission. Expedite leasing offices used for City workforce. "Yes" simplifies street project approval, City property disposition and office leasing. "No" maintains intra-agency consultation for road projects, Council approval for City property dispositions and Council disapproval of office leases.

summary.text: The amendment would simplify the internal review process for street safety projects (such as bike lanes) and let the Department of Transportation Commissioner fast-track infrastructure improvements addressing an identified, immediate safety need, removing a current intra-agency consultation step. It would also fast-track the sale or lease of small City-owned properties, air rights above landmarked City properties, and City office leases -- with City Planning Commission approval replacing the current City Council approval and disapproval role. COGE estimates the change would speed street safety projects by at least 33%, cut the timeline to sell small City land parcels from about seven months to 90 days, and unlock more than $200 million in revenue from surplus lot sales.

measure.yesMeans: Amends the City Charter to simplify review of street safety projects, and fast-track disposition of unused City property and office leases with City Planning Commission approval, removing City Council's current approval role over property dispositions and its ability to disapprove office leases.
measure.noMeans: Leaves the Charter unchanged: street safety projects continue to require intra-agency consultation, and the City Council keeps its approval role over dispositions of City property and its ability to disapprove office leases.

argumentsFor.text: "We're particularly excited about ballot proposals one and three, to speed up outdoor dining permitting and fast-track the installation of street infrastructure that will both save lives and save commuters a great deal of time ... These proposals will save lives," said Ben Furnas, Executive Director of Transportation Alternatives.

"Fast buses can't get here fast enough. By cutting red tape, the Mamdani administration's charter revision will help save riders lots more time even sooner," said Betsy Plum, Executive Director of Riders Alliance.
"An amendment to speed up street safety projects by 33% will save time -- and save lives," said Catherine Vaughan, Executive Director of Abundance New York.

"As a former NYCDOT borough commissioner, I am very excited about COGE's proposals to streamline the approval process for street safety projects. Cutting unnecessary delays will help advance the Mamdani Administration's vision of safer, more livable streets for all New Yorkers, whether they walk, bike, drive, or rely on public transit," said Nivardo Lopez, Former NYC DOT Bronx Borough Commissioner.

argumentsAgainst.text: A spokesperson for City Council Speaker Julie Menin, Henry Robins, said of COGE's ballot package: "In just a few weeks, the commission developed a series of sweeping changes to city government with far-reaching implications for oversight, transparency, and public accountability" -- a concern that applies directly to this proposal's removal of Council approval over City property dispositions and office leases.
